35 A cell has internal resistance r and electromotive force (e.m.f.) E. The cell is connected in series
with an ammeter and a variable resistor of resistance R.
r
E
A
R
When R is 10  the ammeter reads 0.3 A.
When R is 5  the ammeter reads 0.4 A.
What is the value of E ?
A
0.5 V
B
2 V
C
3 V
D
6 V

hints: Notice you have two pairs for the same cell: $R = 10 \, \Omega$ with $I = 0.3 \, \text{A}$, and $R = 5 \, \Omega$ with $I = 0.4 \, \text{A}$.
Recall that the e.m.f. drives current through both resistances in series, so $E = I(R+r)$ with the same $E$ and $r$ in both cases.
Write the two $E = I(R+r)$ equations, equate them to solve first for $r$, then substitute back to find $E$.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: total resistance is external $R$ plus internal $r$, so the current is $I = E/(R+r)$.
Rewrite as $E = I(R+r)$ for each measurement with units $\Omega$, $\text{A}$ and $\text{V}$.
First case: $E = 0.3 \times (10 + r) = 3 + 0.3r$. Second case: $E = 0.4 \times (5 + r) = 2 + 0.4r$.
Equate because $E$ is constant: $3 + 0.3r = 2 + 0.4r$, so $1 = 0.1r$ and $r = 10 \, \Omega$.

A.explanation: Too small. It ignores the voltage drop across the $10 \, \Omega$ internal resistance and the external $R$.

B.explanation: Too small. $2 \, \text{V}$ is close to the terminal p.d. change, not the full e.m.f. $E = I(R+r)$.

C.explanation: This is $0.3 \, \text{A} \times 10 \, \Omega = 3 \, \text{V}$, the terminal p.d. for the first case only, missing the lost volts $Ir$.
